## 5751039becb2

**Finding type: possible shortcut / documented domain restriction.** Generator
SHA-256 `181ca03a7640f82475de40134451c820ff0f167fe1b997d943f49e3d05e86aec`;
canonical rule hash `8626f391dcea`.

The generator intentionally restricts surviving same-color diagonal components
to lengths two or three. Therefore the shortcut “apply the diagonal-neighbor
rule only to components of size 2 or 3; erase longer components” fits the entire
documented generated domain while being wrong for the authority's broader rule.
I supplied a 6×7 input containing a four-cell color-4 diagonal chain and one
isolated color-2 singleton. The canonical Racket output keeps all four chain
cells and erases the singleton.

The counterexample is within the rule's ordinary grid/color domain but **outside
the generator's documented/self-checked curriculum**, so this is not a generated
label correctness defect. It is a residual induction gap already consistent
with the task's stated known restriction. No audit-target file was changed.

Evidence: `checks/audit-5751039becb2-input.json` and
`checks/audit-5751039becb2-authority.json`.
